interface.title: GROMACS Insight Platform (GROMACSInsight)
interface.field: Computational structural biology / molecular dynamics simulation analysis
interface.stage_of_work: Post-simulation triage: checking quality and equilibration of trajectory analysis outputs before deeper, publication-grade analysis
interface.what_it_is_for: Upload GROMACS .xvg/.log analysis outputs (RMSD, RMSF, Rg, SASA, energy…), let the app detect the metric type, explore the traces in interactive plots, then run heuristic equilibration detection, a quality score per file, Welch t-tests between runs and a downloadable Markdown/PDF report.

data.note: I uploaded rmsd_wt.xvg, rmsf_wt.xvg and gyrate_wt.xvg through the sidebar uploader, then added rmsd_mut.xvg and sasa_failed.xvg. Detection results: RMSD 50 rows, RMSF 80 rows, Radius of Gyration 49 rows (the corrupted row at 30000 ps was skipped, which the parsed CSV confirms), rmsd_mut RMSD 50 rows. sasa_failed.xvg gave the warning "Couldn't extract numeric data … skipping those." The app has no built-in sample data.

tree.general: Decide whether simulation runs are equilibrated and trustworthy, find flexible and rigid regions, compare two variants, and record the triage
tree.specific: Triage wild-type and mutant PETase GROMACS outputs (RMSD, RMSF, Rg) with Quick View plots, Analyze (equilibration, quality score, Welch t-test) and report/CSV export

features.name: Multi-file trace overlay with smoothing
features.general: Choose one or more loaded datasets and a shared column and overlay them on one time axis, with an optional moving-average line per series, a unit switch, log scale and point thinning
features.specific: Quick View 'Files to plot' multiselect + 'Column to plot' select drive a Plotly chart ('<col> comparison'), styled by the sidebar Chart type, Time axis unit ps/ns, Overlay moving average (window 2–200), Log scale and Display every Nth frame
steps: pick files in Files to plot (one file gives a single chart, two or more give a comparison chart)
choose the column shared by the files (Backbone, Rg)
toggle Overlay moving average and drag its window
switch the time unit, log scale or Nth-frame thinning
box-zoom and hover to read exact values; double-click to reset
serves_tasks: Plot a trace over time and inspect a suspicious spike
View a second metric to see when it levels off
Smooth the trace and change the axis units and scale
Overlay two runs on one time axis to compare them by eye

features.name: Per-position profile with top-N highlighting
features.general: Show a value for every position along a sequence as bars, colour the N highest, and list them in a ranked table
features.specific: Per-Residue RMSF panel: 'Top N flexible residues' slider (3–25) recolours the top-N bars orange in the RMSF bar chart and fills the 'Top N flexible residues' table (Residue, RMSF nm)
steps: load a per-residue file (detected as RMSF)
drag Top N slider to set how many residues are flagged
read the highlighted bars and the ranked table
box-zoom into a region and hover bars to compare a segment with its neighbours
serves_tasks: Pick out the most flexible positions
Check that a designed segment is less mobile than the rest

features.name: Upload with auto type detection and bad-file warning
features.general: Drop in several files, have each one classified by content, see row counts, and get a warning for files that hold no usable data
features.specific: Sidebar file_uploader (XVG/TXT/LOG) → 'Detected Files' chips '<file> → RMSD (50 rows)'; files with no numeric rows produce the yellow alert "Couldn't extract numeric data from: sasa_failed.xvg — skipping those"; files can be removed with ⊗
steps: click Upload and pick several files
read the detected-type chips with row counts
add more files with + and see any skip warning
remove a file with ⊗ to change the working set
serves_tasks: Load several output files at once and see what type each was recognised as
Add more files and see that unreadable files are reported and left out
Re-run the analysis after changing the file set

features.name: Per-dataset analysis card
features.general: Run one analysis that gives each time series a summary card: mean, spread, confidence interval, a 0–100 quality score, an estimate of when the trace settles, and warnings
features.specific: ▶ Analyze builds an expander per time-series file with Mean, Std Dev, 95% CI and Quality Score tiles, 'Estimated equilibration around …' (in the file's raw time unit, ps, whatever the axis setting), and warning and suggestion boxes; RMSF files get no card
steps: press ▶ Analyze
open a file's card and read the four metric tiles
read the equilibration estimate and warnings
compare the score with the plotted trace before trusting it
serves_tasks: Get a stability score and equilibration estimate for each time series

features.name: Rule-based plain-language explainer over computed numbers
features.general: Type a free-text question about a dataset and get a plain-language answer built by fixed rules from that dataset's computed numbers, not by a language model
features.specific: 'Ask about <file>' text box inside each Analyze card; answers such as 'The composite quality score for this file is 14/100 across 1 metric(s). RMSD stability is low…', captioned 'Rule-based explainer — … no LLM involved.'
steps: press ▶ Analyze and open a file's card
type a question (is this stable? what's the trend?) in Ask about <file>
press Enter and read the explanation
serves_tasks: Ask a plain-language question about a result

features.name: Pairwise comparison of same-type datasets
features.general: Automatically test every pair of datasets that measure the same thing and report the mean difference, test statistic and p-value with a caveat
features.specific: Comparisons section after Analyze: '<a> vs <b> — mean diff, t, p' (Welch t-test) for files with the same detected metric, plus an autocorrelation warning; it disappears when only one file of a type is loaded
steps: load two files of the same metric (rmsd_wt, rmsd_mut)
press ▶ Analyze
read mean diff, t and p in Comparisons
remove one file and re-analyze to drop the comparison
serves_tasks: Test whether two runs differ on the same measurement
Re-run the analysis after changing the file set
